summary: Speaking at a multi-day Memorial Day weekend festival, Indradyumna Swami explains why festivals are essential to Krishna consciousness. The Vaishnava calendar is filled with festivals, and the Nectar of Devotion states it is an offense (aparadha) to ignore them. Festivals mirror the spiritual world — in Goloka Vrindavan "there is a festival every day" — and Krishna (5,000 years ago), then Lord Chaitanya (who uniquely invited even conditioned souls to participate through chanting and dancing), and finally Srila Prabhupada (who introduced the Sunday Love Feast) each brought that festive mood into this world. Festivals matter because ordinary busy life leaves little time for full absorption; a festival delivers a concentrated "big dose" of Krishna consciousness that cleanses the mirror of the heart (ceto-darpana-marjanam), like spring cleaning, turning slow incremental progress into a quantum leap. He urges everyone not to hold back but to give themselves fully to chanting, dancing, hearing, and honoring prasadam.
key_points: The Vaishnava calendar is full of festivals; the Nectar of Devotion says ignoring them is an offense (aparadha).
Festivals reflect the eternal festive mood of Goloka Vrindavan, where every day is a festival.
Krishna, Lord Chaitanya (who let conditioned souls join through the holy name), and Prabhupada (the Sunday Love Feast) each introduced this festive mood to the world.
Ordinary life leaves little time for absorption; a festival gives a concentrated 'big dose' of Krishna consciousness.
Chanting cleanses the mirror of the heart (ceto-darpana-marjanam) — a festival is like spring cleaning.
Don't be shy: give yourself fully to the process — chanting, dancing, hearing, and prasadam.
references: Nectar of Devotion (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu) — it is an offense (aparadha) not to observe the festivals of the Vaishnava calendar.
Siksastakam, verse 1 — 'ceto-darpana-marjanam...'; chanting cleanses the mirror of the heart.
Siksastakam, verse 7 — 'yugayitam nimesena...'; in separation a moment feels like twelve years, tears flowing like torrents of rain.
Brahma-samhita — Goloka Vrindavan, where 'all walking is dancing and all talking is singing' and there is a festival every day.
Sri Chaitanya-caritamrita, Madhya 19.53 — Rupa Goswami's prayer 'namo maha-vadanyaya krsna-prema-pradaya te...'; Chaitanya is the most munificent incarnation, freely bestowing krsna-prema.
Songs of the Vaishnava Acaryas (Srila Prabhupada's Introduction) — 'we must always merge in the transcendental mellow of kirtana-rasa', the safest situation in the material world.
stories: Cleaning the car mirror — the speaker sprays and wipes every window before driving, as chanting cleans the ever-dirtying mirror of the heart.
Spring cleaning — after a musty winter you throw open the windows and scrub; a festival is spring cleaning for the heart.
The unwashed boy — filthy and matted, he said 'I like to keep life's experiences with me,' illustrating a heart that is never cleansed.
The doctor's injection — busy life leaves us treading water, so a festival is a big dose that cures the disease of material existence.
Krishna returning to Vrindavan — the villagers stand like wooden dolls in separation when He leaves for the forest and celebrate every evening when He returns.
Prabhupada and the GBC on the Mayapur festival — told the expense did not matter because coming together to chant is so important.
Vishnujana Swami's chastisement — 'the only thing you haven't done is given your life fully to Krishna.'
quotes: It does not matter. It is so important that we all come together like this and chant Hare Krishna and hear the glories of Lord Chaitanya.
No, I like to keep life's experiences with me.
The only thing you haven't done is given your life fully to Krishna.
